items.he_draft: חוקרים נתנו לכל אחד מן המשתתפים בניסוי קופסת פרלינים. למחצית מן המשתתפים נאמר שהפרלינים הוכנו בעבודת יד בסדנה קטנה, ולמחצית האחרת נאמר שהם הוכנו במפעל גדול. למעשה, הפרלינים בכל הקופסאות היו זהים. לאחר שטעמו מהם, דירג כל משתתף עד כמה הם טעימים. איזו מן ההשערות שלהלן בדקו החוקרים? (1) אנשים מעדיפים פרלינים הנמכרים בקופסה על פני פרלינים הנמכרים בתפזורת (2) מה שנאמר לאנשים על אופן הכנתו של מזון משפיע על מידת טעמו בעיניהם (3) מזון המוכן בעבודת יד בסדנאות קטנות טעים יותר ממזון המוכן במפעלים גדולים (4) אנשים הטועמים מזון לפני שהם מדרגים אותו מדרגים אותו גבוה יותר מאנשים שאינם טועמים אותו
items.stem: Researchers gave each of the participants in an experiment a box of chocolates. Half of the participants were told that the chocolates had been made by hand in a small workshop, and the other half were told that they had been made in a large factory. In fact, the chocolates in all the boxes were the same. After tasting them, each participant rated how tasty the chocolates were. Which of the following hypotheses did the researchers test?
options: People prefer chocolates that are sold in a box to chocolates that are sold loose
What people are told about how a food was made influences how tasty it seems to them
Food that is made by hand in small workshops is tastier than food that is made in large factories
People who taste a food before rating it rate it higher than people who do not taste it
items.explanation: The only thing that differs between the two halves is what they were told about how the chocolates were made, and what is measured is how tasty they seemed. The chocolates themselves were the same, so (3), which is about real differences between the chocolates, is not what was tested; everyone received a box (1) and everyone tasted (4).

items.he_draft: במשך שנים רבות האמינו החקלאים של כפר מסוים שהכתמים הכהים המופיעים על התאנים במטעיהם נגרמים בשל ערפל הבוקר, ושלצרעות הזעירות הנמצאות במטעים באותה עונה אין בכך כל חלק. תצפיות מאוחרות יותר הראו שאמונה זו מוטעית. איזו מן התוצאות שלהלן לא הייתה מראה שהאמונה מוטעית? (1) על תאנים שנקטפו ונאכלו לפני עונת הערפל לא היו כתמים (2) בשנה שבה לא הגיעו הצרעות למטעים בשל כפור מאוחר, כמעט לא היו כתמים, אף שהערפל היה כרגיל (3) במטע במורד ההר, שאין בו לעולם ערפל בוקר, היו כתמים על רבות מן התאנים (4) חקלאי שכיסה חלק מעציו ברשתות דקות מצא כתמים רק על העצים שלא כוסו
items.stem: For many years, the farmers of a certain village believed that the dark spots that appear on the figs in their orchards are caused by the morning fog, and that the tiny wasps found in the orchards in the same season play no part in this. Later observations showed that this belief was wrong. Which of the following results would not have shown that the belief was wrong?
options: Figs that were picked and eaten before the season of fog did not have spots
In a year in which the wasps did not reach the orchards because of a late frost, there were almost no spots, although the fog was as usual
In an orchard on the slope of the mountain, where there is never morning fog, many of the figs had spots
A farmer who covered part of his trees with fine nets found spots only on the trees that were not covered
items.explanation: Figs picked before the season of fog are not what the belief is about: with no fog, the belief also predicts no spots, so this result fits it. (2) shows fog without spots when the wasps were absent, (3) shows spots without fog, and (4) shows that the nets, which kept the wasps away but not the fog, prevented the spots.

items.style_donor: Summer 2026 §2 Q4 (waiting in a lecturer's office)
items.he_draft: מחקר מצא שכאשר מושמעת מוזיקת רקע, אנשים מבצעים משימות חוזרות טוב יותר מאשר בשקט, ואילו משימות הדורשות קריאה מדוקדקת הם מבצעים גרוע יותר מאשר בשקט. איזו מן ההשערות שלהלן אינה מסבירה ממצא זה? (1) מוזיקה מעוררת את המאזין. העוררות מונעת את הישנוניות שגורמת עבודה חד-גונית, אך היא מפריעה לריכוז שקריאה מדוקדקת דורשת (2) האזנה למוזיקה משתמשת באותן יכולות שמשמשות בקריאה, ולכן המוזיקה מפריעה לקריאה, ואילו בעבודה חד-גונית המוזיקה מפחיתה שעמום (3) מוזיקה מסיטה חלק מתשומת הלב מן המשימה, וזה פוגע בביצוע כל משימה, אך במשימה חד-גונית, הדורשת מעט תשומת לב, הפגיעה קטנה יותר (4) מוזיקה משפרת את מצב הרוח, ומצב רוח טוב עוזר במשימות פשוטות אך גורם לאנשים לקרוא בפחות קפידה
items.stem: A study found that when background music is played, people perform repetitive tasks better than they do in silence, whereas they perform tasks that require careful reading worse than they do in silence. Which of the following hypotheses does not explain this finding?
options: Music arouses the listener. Arousal prevents the sleepiness that monotonous work causes, but it disturbs the concentration that careful reading requires
Listening to music uses the same abilities that are used in reading, and therefore music disturbs reading, while in monotonous work the music reduces boredom
Music draws part of the attention away from the task, and this harms the performance of every task, but in a monotonous task, which requires little attention, the harm is smaller
Music improves the mood, and a good mood helps in simple tasks but causes people to read less carefully
items.explanation: A harm that is smaller in monotonous tasks is still a harm, so it cannot explain why these tasks are performed better with music than in silence. (1), (2) and (4) each give a reason for both halves of the finding.

items.he_draft: האקולוגית הררי ספרה, במשך שתים עשרה שנה, את קיני השחפיות בשני חלקים של אי: על מצוקי חופו הצפוני ועל חוף החול שבדרומו. היא מצאה שעל המצוקים יש הרבה יותר קינים מאשר על החוף, ושההפרש בין שני החלקים משתנה משנה לשנה: עלייה במספר השועלים באי כמעט אינה משפיעה על מספר הקינים על המצוקים, אך גורמת לירידה חדה במספר הקינים על החוף. לפי ממצאיה, אם בשנת 1987 היו באי יותר שועלים מאשר בשנת 1986, סביר ש- (1) מספר הקינים על המצוקים בשנת 1987 היה נמוך מאשר בשנת 1986 (2) מספר הקינים על החוף בשנת 1987 היה גבוה ממספר הקינים על המצוקים באותה שנה (3) בשנת 1987 מספר הקינים על החוף היה זהה למספרם בשנת 1986, אך על המצוקים הוא היה נמוך בהרבה (4) הפער במספר הקינים בין המצוקים לחוף היה גדול יותר בשנת 1987 מאשר בשנת 1986
items.stem: The ecologist Harari counted, over twelve years, the nests of terns in two parts of an island: on the cliffs of its northern coast and on the sandy shore of its southern coast. She found that there are many more nests on the cliffs than on the shore, and that the difference between the two parts changes from year to year: a rise in the number of foxes on the island hardly affects the number of nests on the cliffs, but leads to a sharp drop in the number of nests on the shore. According to her findings, if there were more foxes on the island in 1987 than in 1986, it is likely that -
options: the number of nests on the cliffs in 1987 was lower than in 1986
the number of nests on the shore in 1987 was higher than the number of nests on the cliffs in that year
in 1987 the number of nests on the shore was the same as in 1986, but on the cliffs it was much lower
the gap in the number of nests between the cliffs and the shore was greater in 1987 than in 1986
items.explanation: More foxes leave the cliffs almost unchanged and cut the shore sharply, so the gap grows. (1) changes the part that foxes hardly affect, (3) swaps the roles of the two parts, and (2) contradicts the finding that the cliffs have far more nests, which is even truer after a rise in foxes.

items.he_draft: חוקרים שעקבו במשך כמה שנים אחר שיח מדבר מסוים מצאו שזרעיו, המכוסים בקליפה קשה, נובטים רק לאחר שעברו במערכת העיכול של צבי, המרככת את הקליפה. השיח נושא פרי פעם אחת בשנה, בתחילת הקיץ, והפרי נושר לאדמה בתוך כשלושה שבועות. צבאים מעדיפים לאכול עשב, והם אוכלים את פרי השיח רק כאשר קשה למצוא עשב. על סמך הפסקה, באיזו מן השנים שלהלן סביר ביותר ששיחים חדשים רבים יתחילו לצמוח? (1) בשנה שבה השיחים נשאו יותר פרי מן הרגיל (2) בשנה שבה היה מעט עשב בסוף החורף (3) בשנה שבה היה מעט עשב בתחילת הקיץ (4) בשנה שבה היו באזור יותר צבאים מן הרגיל
items.stem: Researchers who followed a certain desert shrub for several years found that its seeds, which are covered with a hard coat, germinate only after they have passed through the digestive system of a gazelle, which softens the coat. The shrub bears fruit once a year, at the beginning of summer, and the fruit falls to the ground within about three weeks. Gazelles prefer to eat grass, and they eat the fruit of the shrub only when grass is hard to find. Based on the paragraph, in which of the following years is it most likely that many new shrubs will begin to grow?
options: A year in which the shrubs bore more fruit than usual
A year in which there was little grass at the end of winter
A year in which there was little grass at the beginning of summer
A year in which there were more gazelles in the area than in other years
items.explanation: Seeds germinate only after a gazelle has eaten the fruit, gazelles eat it only when grass is scarce, and the fruit is there only in early summer. (2) has scarce grass at a time when there is no fruit, and (1) and (4) are a step short: with plenty of grass, the gazelles would not eat the fruit.

items.he_draft: תנועת נוער בוחרת מדריכים למחנה הקיץ שלה. כל מדריך שנבחר חייב לקיים לפחות אחד משני התנאים הבאים: א. יש לו ניסיון של שנתיים לפחות כמדריך. ב. הוא סיים קורס עזרה ראשונה והוא מבוגר מגיל 20. באיזו מן הקבוצות שלהלן יש מועמד שאינו יכול להיבחר? (1) איה, 19, בעלת ניסיון של שלוש שנים; גדי, 23, בעל ניסיון של שנה, שסיים קורס עזרה ראשונה; רונית, 20, בעלת ניסיון של שנתיים מלאות (2) אלי, 24, בעל ניסיון של ארבע שנים; הודיה, 20, בעלת ניסיון של שנה, שסיימה קורס עזרה ראשונה; יאיר, 19, בעל ניסיון של שנתיים (3) דפנה, 22, בעלת ניסיון של שנתיים; שאול, 25, בעל ניסיון של חמש שנים; מור, 19, בעלת ניסיון של שלוש שנים (4) עדי, 26, שאין לו ניסיון אך סיים קורס עזרה ראשונה; בן, 21, בעל ניסיון של שנתיים; נילי, 20, בעלת ניסיון של שלוש שנים
items.stem:
A youth movement chooses counselors for its summer camp. Every counselor who is chosen must meet at least one of the following two conditions:
A. He has at least two years of experience as a counselor.
B. He has completed a first-aid course and is older than 20.
In which of the following groups of candidates is there a candidate who cannot be chosen?
options: Aya, 19, with three years of experience; Gadi, 23, with one year of experience, who has completed a first-aid course; Ronit, 20, with two full years of experience
Eli, 24, with four years of experience; Hodaya, 20, with one year of experience, who has completed a first-aid course; Yair, 19, with two years of experience
Dafna, 22, with two years of experience; Shaul, 25, with five years of experience; Mor, 19, with three years of experience
Adi, 26, who has no experience but has completed a first-aid course; Ben, 21, with two years of experience; Nili, 20, with three years of experience
items.explanation: Hodaya has only one year of experience, and although she has completed a first-aid course, she is not older than 20, so she meets neither condition. In (1) Gadi and in (4) Adi lack the experience but meet condition B, since each has completed the course and is older than 20; in (3) every candidate has at least two years of experience.

items.he_draft: ארבעה מועמדים ניגשו למשרה של מדריך במוזיאון עירוני. אלה היו התוצאות: - אלדד, הדובר אנגלית וצרפתית, התקבל לעבודה. - ציפי, הדוברת אנגלית, התקבלה לעבודה. - אורנה, הדוברת רוסית, לא התקבלה. - מוטי, הדובר רוסית וספרדית, התקבל לעבודה. הערה: אף אחד מארבעת המועמדים אינו דובר שפה אחרת מלבד השפות שצוינו לעיל. איזו מן הדרישות שלהלן לא ייתכן שהייתה הדרישה לקבלה לעבודה? (1) כל מועמד הדובר שתי שפות מתקבל, וגם כל מועמד הדובר אנגלית מתקבל (2) כל המועמדים מתקבלים, חוץ מאלה הדוברים שפה אחת בלבד ושפה זו אינה אנגלית (3) מועמד מתקבל רק אם הוא דובר יותר משפה אחת או שאינו דובר אנגלית כלל (4) מועמד שאינו דובר אנגלית אינו מתקבל, אלא אם כן הוא דובר ספרדית
items.stem:
Four candidates applied for a job as a guide at a city museum. These were the results:
- Eldad, who speaks English and French, was accepted for the job.
- Tzipi, who speaks English, was accepted for the job.
- Orna, who speaks Russian, was not accepted.
- Moti, who speaks Russian and Spanish, was accepted for the job.
Note: none of the four candidates speaks any language other than those listed above. Which of the following could not have been the requirement for being accepted for the job?
options: Any candidate who speaks two languages is accepted, and any candidate who speaks English is accepted as well
All of the candidates are accepted, except those who speak one language only and that language is not English
A candidate is accepted only if he speaks more than one language or does not speak English at all
A candidate who does not speak English is not accepted, unless he speaks Spanish
items.explanation: Under (3) Tzipi, who speaks English and nothing else, could not be accepted, yet she was. Each of the other requirements fits all four results.

items.he_draft: אמנון, ברכה וגילה גרים בבניין בן שלוש קומות, כל אחד בקומה אחרת, לאו דווקא בסדר זה. כל אחד מהם מגדל אחת מחיות המחמד הבאות: חתול, כלב וארנב. נתון: א. ברכה גרה בקומה הסמוכה לקומתו של בעל הכלב. ב. בעל הארנב גר בקומה השנייה. איזו מן הטענות שלהלן נכונה בהכרח? (1) גילה היא בעלת החתול (2) אמנון גר בקומה השלישית של הבניין (3) אמנון אינו בעל הארנב (4) גילה אינה בעלת הכלב
items.stem: Amnon, Bracha and Gila live in a three-story building, one on each floor, not necessarily in that order. Each of them keeps one of these pets: a cat, a dog and a rabbit. Given: A. Bracha lives on a floor adjacent to the floor of the dog's owner. B. The owner of the rabbit lives on the second floor. Which of the following is necessarily true?
options: Gila is the owner of the cat
Amnon lives on the third floor of the building
Amnon is not the owner of the rabbit
Gila is not the owner of the dog
items.explanation: If Bracha lived on the first or third floor, the only floor adjacent to hers would be the second, whose tenant owns the rabbit, not the dog; so Bracha lives on the second floor and owns the rabbit. Amnon and Gila may be on either of the other floors, with either the cat or the dog.

items.stem: Two novels and two cookbooks stand on a shelf in places 1 to 4, numbered from left to right. It is known that the two cookbooks do not stand next to each other. Which of the following additional facts would make it possible to determine with certainty the type of every book?
options: Book 3 is a novel
Book 4 is a cookbook
Book 1 is a novel
No book stands next to a book of its own type
items.explanation: The cookbooks can stand in places 1 and 3, 1 and 4, or 2 and 4; a novel in place 1 leaves only 2 and 4. (1) and (2) each leave 1 and 4 or 2 and 4, and (4) leaves 1 and 3 or 2 and 4.

items.he_draft: הדברים שנאמרו בשיחה הבאה סותרים זה את זה. צילה: ״יגאל משאיל את ספריו רק לאנשים המבוגרים ממנו.״ אלי: ״אני צעיר מיגאל.״ אורנה: ״אני מבוגרת מאלי וצעירה מצילה.״ יגאל: ״השאלתי ספרים לצילה, לאורנה ולאלי.״ בלי דבריו של איזה מן הדוברים עדיין תהיה בשיחה סתירה? (1) צילה (2) אלי (3) אורנה (4) יגאל
items.stem: The statements made in the following conversation contradict one another. Tzila: "Yigal lends his books only to people who are older than he is." Eli: "I am younger than Yigal." Orna: "I am older than Eli and younger than Tzila." Yigal: "I have lent books to Tzila, to Orna and to Eli." Without which speaker's statement would the conversation still contain a contradiction?
options: Tzila
Eli
Orna
Yigal
items.explanation: Tzila's and Yigal's statements together make Eli older than Yigal, while Eli says he is younger; Orna's statement plays no part in this. Removing Tzila, Eli or Yigal removes one part of the contradiction.

items.he_draft: עינת, חגי ומוטי היו צריכים לבחור היכן יבלה הצוות שלהם יום גיבוש: בגן החיות, בחוף הים או במוזיאון המדע. כל אחד מהם הביע משאלה. עינת: ״הייתי רוצה שנלך לחוף הים.״ חגי: ״לא אכפת לי לאן נלך, ובלבד שלא יהיה זה גן החיות.״ מוטי: ״אהיה מרוצה אם נלך למוזיאון המדע, או אם חגי יהיה מרוצה.״ הצוות הלך לאחד משלושת המקומות, ובדיוק אחד מן השלושה לא זכה שמשאלתו תתקיים. איזו מן הטענות שלהלן אפשרית? (1) הצוות הלך לחוף הים (2) משאלתו של מוטי לא התקיימה (3) הצוות הלך למוזיאון המדע (4) חגי היה היחיד שמשאלתו לא התקיימה
items.stem: Einat, Hagai and Moti had to choose where their team would spend a day out: at the zoo, at the beach or at the science museum. Each of them expressed a wish. Einat: "I would like us to go to the beach." Hagai: "I do not mind where we go, as long as it is not the zoo." Moti: "I will be pleased if we go to the science museum, or if Hagai is pleased." The team went to one of the three places, and exactly one of the three did not get his wish. Which of the following is possible?
options: The team went to the beach
Moti did not get his wish
The team went to the science museum
Hagai was the only one who did not get his wish
items.explanation: At the museum Einat is disappointed while Hagai and Moti are pleased, so exactly one wish fails. At the beach everyone is pleased. Hagai's wish fails only at the zoo, and there Einat's and Moti's wishes fail too; Moti's wish fails only when Hagai's does, which again happens only at the zoo.

items.he_draft: חמישה מתמודדים משתתפים בחידון טלוויזיה: שרית, אמנון, יגאל, ציפי ואלדד. בכל סיבוב מתמודדים שני מתמודדים. המפסיד עוזב את החידון, והמנצח מתמודד בסיבוב הבא מול מתמודד שעוד לא התמודד, עד הסיבוב הרביעי והאחרון. ידוע הכלל הבא: אם שרית מתמודדת מול מתמודד שבסיבוב הקודם התמודד מול אמנון, שרית מפסידה; בכל מקרה אחר שרית מנצחת. אם שרית התמודדה בסיבוב הראשון של החידון, אז - (1) היא הפסידה בסיבוב השני (2) היא ניצחה בסיבוב האחרון (3) היא הפסידה בסיבוב הראשון (4) היא הפסידה בסיבוב האחרון
items.stem: Five contestants take part in a television quiz: Sarit, Amnon, Yigal, Tzipi and Eldad. In each round two contestants compete. The loser leaves the quiz, and the winner competes in the next round against a contestant who has not yet competed, until the fourth and last round. The following rule is known: if Sarit competes against a contestant who, in the previous round, competed against Amnon, Sarit loses; in every other case Sarit wins. If Sarit competed in the first round of the quiz, then -
options: she lost in the second round
she won the last round
she lost in the first round
she lost in the last round
items.explanation: Every opponent Sarit meets after the first round is a newcomer who did not compete in the previous round, and in the first round there was no previous round; so the rule never makes her lose, and she wins every round including the last.

passages.he_draft: שאלות ששונו: 1. איזו מן הטענות שלהלן קרובה ביותר במשמעותה למשפט ״הדפוס, עם זאת, הוא נטייה ולא חוק ... שהדפוס צופה״ (פסקה 1)? 2. מדוע נוטים בעלי חיים גדולים להתקטן באיים, לפי ההסבר המקובל ביותר (פסקה 2)? (3) משום שכאשר המזון אוזל, הפרטים הזקוקים לפחות מזון סבירים יותר לשרוד ולהעמיד צאצאים (4) משום שהמזון הגדל באיים איכותו ירודה מזו של המזון ביבשה, וגוף גדול אינו יכול להתקיים ממנו 4. איזו מן הטענות שלהלן אינה נכונה לגבי ההסבר מן הטורפים (פסקה 3)? 5. איזה מן הממצאים שלהלן במחקר המתואר בפסקה 4 היה תומך בהסבר מן הטורפים? (2) גודל הלטאות בכל אי תואם במידה רבה את מספר החרקים שהן ניזונות מהם באותו אי 6. איזו מן הטענות שלהלן מבטאת בצורה הטובה ביותר את הרעיון המרכזי של הקטע? (2) גודלו של בעל חיים אינו קבוע, אלא הוא פשרה בין לחצים שהתנאים באי יכולים לשנות
passages.title: Passage 1
facts: Island animals often differ in size from mainland relatives: large species tend to become smaller and small species larger (the "island rule"), with many exceptions.
Dwarf elephants lived on Mediterranean islands including Sicily and Malta; the smallest stood about a meter or less at the shoulder.
The Flores giant rat (Papagomys armandvillei) is several times heavier than the common rat.
The pattern was described by J. Bristol Foster (Nature, 1964) and is known as the island rule (Foster's rule).
Limited food and the absence of large predators are the two standard explanations of the island rule.
The lizard study in paragraph 4 is an unnamed illustrative study, not attributed to real researchers.
paragraphs: Biologists have long observed that island animals often differ in size from their closest relatives on the mainland, and in a predictable direction: species that are large on the mainland tend to become smaller on islands, while species that are small tend to become larger. The fossil record offers striking cases of the first kind. Several Mediterranean islands, Sicily and Malta among them, were once home to dwarf elephants, some of which stood barely a meter high at the shoulder. A living case of the second kind is a rat on the Indonesian island of Flores that weighs several times as much as the common rat. The pattern was first described in 1964 by the zoologist J. Bristol Foster, and it is known today as "the island rule." The pattern, however, is a tendency rather than a law: a great many island species do not differ in size from their mainland relatives at all, and a few have changed in the direction opposite to the one that the pattern predicts.

The most widely accepted explanation concerns food. An island offers a limited supply of food, and its animals cannot move elsewhere when that supply runs short. A large body requires a great deal of food, whereas a smaller individual of the same species can get through a lean season on what remains. Over many generations, therefore, smaller individuals are more likely to survive and leave offspring, and the population as a whole becomes smaller. Some researchers have refined this explanation. According to them, what matters is not the area of the island but the amount of food it provides for each animal: a large island consisting mostly of bare rock may favor small bodies more strongly than a small island covered with dense vegetation.

A second explanation looks not to food but to enemies. Remote islands often have few large predators or none, since such predators need extensive hunting grounds and seldom cross the sea. On the mainland, being small helps an animal to escape by hiding in cracks and burrows, while being very large protects a grazing animal, since few predators can overcome it. Where there are no predators, both advantages lose their value, and body size is free to shift toward whatever suits local conditions best. This explanation accounts for both directions of change by a single cause, whereas the explanation from food is more convincing for the shrinking of large animals than for the growth of small ones. On the other hand, it predicts a change in size on every island that lacks predators, although many such islands are home to species whose size has not changed.

A team of biologists compared the two explanations on a chain of small islands inhabited by a single species of lizard. A predatory snake lives on some of the islands but not on others, and the islands also differ in their vegetation, and hence in the number of insects on which the lizards feed. The researchers reasoned that if the explanation from predators were correct, the lizards on the snake-free islands should differ in size from those on the other islands even where the supply of insects was similar. In fact, the lizards' size corresponded closely to the supply of insects, whereas the presence of snakes made almost no difference. The researchers concluded that on these islands, at least, food is the decisive factor. They added a caution, however: since the snakes reached the islands relatively recently, the lizards may not yet have had time to respond to them.

Neither explanation, then, turns the island pattern into a law. What the island cases do show is something more general: the size of an animal, which we tend to regard as a fixed feature of its species, is in fact a compromise among competing pressures, such as the need for food, the danger from predators and the demands of the climate. When life on an island shifts the balance among these pressures, size shifts with it, and the fossil record suggests that on some islands this happened within a few thousand years.

questions.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the sentence "The pattern, however, is a tendency rather than a law … the pattern predicts" (paragraph 1)?
options: Not every island species conforms to the pattern: many have not changed in size at all, and some have even changed in the opposite direction
Most island species conform to the pattern, and those that do not conform to it have changed in size in the opposite direction
Since many island species have not changed in size, the direction of change that the pattern predicts is often the wrong one
A few island species have changed in size in the predicted direction, but a great many have not changed in size at all
questions.explanation: The sentence names two exceptions: many species that did not change and a few that changed the other way. (2) adds "most" and merges the two groups, (3) turns "no change" into evidence of the wrong direction, and (4) attaches "a few" to the species that follow the pattern.

questions.stem: Why do large animals tend to become smaller on islands, according to the most widely accepted explanation (paragraph 2)?
options: Because the area of an island is too small to hold animals of a large size
Because on an island, smaller animals find it easier to hide from predators
Because when food runs short, the individuals that need less food are more likely to survive and leave offspring
Because the food that grows on islands is of poorer quality than the food on the mainland, and a large body cannot be sustained by it
questions.explanation: The paragraph links size to the amount of food: a smaller body gets through a lean season, and over generations the population shrinks. (1) is what the refinement of this explanation denies, (2) belongs to the other explanation (paragraph 3), and (4) speaks of quality, which the paragraph never mentions.

questions.stem: Two populations of the same species of wild goat live on two islands of equal area. The goats on the first island are considerably smaller than those on the second. According to the refinement that some researchers proposed to the explanation from food, which of the following could explain this?
options: The first island is farther from the mainland than the second
The first island provides less food for each goat than the second
There are more predators on the first island than on the second
The second island consists mostly of bare rock, whereas the first is covered with dense vegetation
questions.explanation: According to the refinement of the explanation from food, the food available to each animal, not the island's area, decides how strongly small bodies are favored. (4) reverses the two islands, and (1) and (3) name factors the hypothesis does not use; more predators would, if anything, favor larger bodies.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not correct regarding the explanation from predators (paragraph 3)?
options: It holds that the absence of predators can account both for the growth of small animals and for the shrinking of large ones
It assumes that a very large body can protect a grazing animal from predators
It predicts that species living on islands without predators will change in size
It is more convincing for the shrinking of large animals than for the growth of small ones
questions.explanation: The paragraph says this of the explanation from food, and presents the predator explanation's merit as covering both directions. (1), (2) and (3) are each stated in the paragraph.

questions.stem: Which of the following findings in the study described in paragraph 4 would have supported the explanation from predators?
options: Lizards on the snake-free islands differ in size from lizards on islands with snakes that have a similar supply of insects
The size of the lizards on each island corresponds closely to the number of insects on which they feed on that island
The snakes reached the islands only a relatively short time ago
The lizards are of the same size on all of the islands in the chain
questions.explanation: The researchers said the predator explanation required a size difference between snake-free and snake islands even where food was similar. (2) is the actual finding, which supports the food explanation; (3) is the researchers' caution, which may excuse the predator explanation but does not support it; (4) supports neither explanation.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the text?
options: Animals on islands always change in size, in whichever direction the local supply of food dictates
The size of an animal is not fixed, but is a compromise among pressures that the conditions on an island can change
The explanation from food has been shown to be correct, and the explanation from predators has been refuted
Island animals are smaller than their mainland relatives because islands offer less food and fewer predators
questions.explanation: The last paragraph draws the general lesson that the whole passage builds toward. (1) says "always," which paragraph 1 denies; (3) overstates a study whose conclusion is limited to "these islands, at least"; (4) ignores the small animals that grow larger.
